## Research Report: Does Olive Oil Reduce Stroke Risk?

**Conclusion:** The evidence broadly supports your view — olive oil consumption, especially extra-virgin olive oil, is associated with a reduced risk of stroke — but with important caveats about causality and study design.

### Supporting Evidence

**1. The PREDIMED Randomized Controlled Trial:** This landmark trial randomized ~7,447 participants to a Mediterranean diet supplemented with extra-virgin olive oil (~1 liter/week), a Mediterranean diet with nuts, or a control low-fat diet. The olive oil group saw a ~30% reduction in the composite endpoint of stroke, heart attack, or cardiovascular death, with stroke being the primary driver of the effect (stroke risk dropped from 3.0% to 1.7% over 5 years). This is the strongest evidence because it is an intervention trial, not merely observational. ([PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29897866/), [ScienceDaily](https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2013/02/130225181536.htm))

**2. Meta-analyses of cohort and case-control studies:** A meta-analysis found olive oil consumption associated with lower risk of both CVD and stroke, with maximum benefit at 20–30 g/day (~1.5–2 tablespoons). The association appeared stronger for virgin olive oil. ([British Journal of Nutrition](https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/british-journal-of-nutrition/article/olive-oil-consumption-and-risk-of-chd-andor-stroke-a-metaanalysis-of-casecontrol-cohort-and-intervention-studies/79A90337470271D8A8CE2FDC77BD869E), [Frontiers in Nutrition](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/nutrition/articles/10.3389/fnut.2022.1041203/full))

### Caveats and Counterarguments

- **PREDIMED was retracted and republished** due to irregularities in randomization at some sites, though the reanalysis confirmed the original findings. ([The BMJ](https://www.bmj.com/content/364/bmj.l341))
- **Observational studies cannot prove causation.** As one researcher noted, "People who use a lot of olive oil may be very different from people who don't" — confounding factors like overall diet and lifestyle may explain part of the association. ([Tribune](https://tribune.com.pk/story/190170/olive-oil-lovers-show-lower-stroke-risk/))
- The benefit appears specific to **extra-virgin olive oil**, which is richer in polyphenols and antioxidants than refined olive oil. ([Nature](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41430-022-01221-3))

### Bottom Line

Your claim is well-supported by both the best available RCT (PREDIMED) and multiple meta-analyses. The evidence is strongest for extra-virgin olive oil consumed at moderate levels (~20–30 g/day) within a Mediterranean dietary pattern. However, the evidence is not airtight — the PREDIMED trial had methodological issues (later corrected), and observational data carry inherent confounding limitations.
